questions.prompt: A prospect says her current software’s support has been excellent. You’ve heard elsewhere that its support is weak. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her what you’ve heard so she can weigh it before she renews
Agree it’s a strength, then show where Momence fits her needs better
Say Momence’s support is faster, without getting into specifics
Skip the topic of support and move the demo straight to pricing

questions.reveal: Several competitors out-rate us on day-to-day service. Grant what’s true and move to where Momence is stronger for her.

questions.prompt: Which kind of competitor claim is safe to make on a demo?

options.text: A line other AEs use that prospects tend to react well to hearing
Something a former customer of theirs told you on a past demo
A comparison you remember from a blog post or a review site
A fee taken from the competitor’s own published pricing or proposal

questions.reveal: Only first-party facts and what the prospect tells you about their own experience. Everything else stays out.

questions.prompt: An owner on Mariana Tek asks why she would switch to its sister company’s product. What’s your best move?

options.text: Ask what isn’t working for her today, then show where Momence fits
Explain that Mariana Tek is built for big franchises, not her size
Tell her Momence is the newer and better product of the two brands
Say it’s much the same software, so switching over will be simple

questions.reveal: Don’t knock it and don’t lean on the franchise framing, which is still being confirmed. Let her pain drive the demo.

questions.prompt: A Mariana Tek studio has no schedule on its website; new clients have to book through the app. What do you show?

options.text: The branded app, so her clients can keep booking the same way
The AI agent, so app questions get answered around the clock
A schedule on her own site that shows classes and drop-in prices
The referral program, so members invite friends through the app

questions.reveal: A new person can see classes, prices and instructors straight away and book without downloading anything first.

questions.prompt: A MindBody owner says, “I loved it as a client and a teacher. It’s the back end that drives me crazy.” What’s your next move?

options.text: Show the client checkout first, since that’s where Momence wins
Agree MindBody is outdated, then run the full feature tour for her
Ask what in the back end costs her the most, then demo against it
Move to pricing, since back-end pain means she’s ready to switch

questions.reveal: She told you the strength and the pain in one line. Dig into the pain before you share a screen.

questions.prompt: Per the CC5 battle card, which MindBody fee does Momence not charge?

options.text: A marketplace fee on new clients who find the studio via its app
A setup fee for each new staff account the studio adds to it
A monthly fee for every class the studio lists on its schedule
A per-message charge on the in-app notifications clients get

questions.reveal: It’s on new clients who come through the MindBody app. Ask if they know what it adds up to in a year.

questions.prompt: A MindBody prospect says her booking widget feels like a window dropped into her site, and it takes clients off the page. What do you show?

options.text: The free Momence app, so clients book there instead of her site
The community page, so clients see posts before they book a class
The ads manager, so more traffic reaches the widget she has today
The schedule plugin styled to her brand, then the one-page checkout

questions.reveal: The plugin can be styled to match the studio, and checkout is one page with no account to create.

questions.prompt: A MindBody prospect worries that clients who download the free Momence app will see other studios. What’s accurate?

options.text: They’ll see nearby studios unless she pays for the branded app
It’s no marketplace; clients see only studios they’ve bought from
They’ll see other studios, but only ones in a different city
They’ll see other studios until she turns that off in settings

questions.reveal: No other studio can advertise to her clients in the free app. That’s a real difference from a marketplace app.

questions.prompt: A WellnessLiving prospect says she’s fairly sure she has no contract. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her WellnessLiving often uses three-year contracts anyway
Assume she’s free to switch and plan the move for next month
Offer extra free months to cover any contract she might find
Ask her to check her agreement and renewal date before planning

questions.reveal: You don’t know their contract terms, and guessing is a knock. Her own agreement is the source.

questions.prompt: A WellnessLiving owner says her deciding need is booking private events online with a deposit, then the balance later. You haven’t seen it demoed. What do you do?

options.text: Say yes, it’s standard, and move on to pricing and the contract
Confirm how Momence builds it, then demo it before you close
Tell her WellnessLiving can’t do it, so any switch is a step up
Suggest she keep invoicing those events by hand through Square

questions.reveal: In one cycle this need was agreed to and never shown across four calls. Prove the deciding need on screen.

questions.prompt: A Glofox owner says his price has gone up since he joined. Which question fits the stance?

options.text: Did you know Glofox has hidden fees that studios find out later?
Have you heard how many studios are leaving Glofox this year?
What did it move to, and how much notice did they give you?
Want to hear how our prices have held for every customer?

questions.reveal: He answers it from his own experience. Hidden-fee hearsay and price promises are both unverified.

questions.prompt: A Glofox owner says there’s no direct sign-up link; the booking widget has to be embedded on his site. What do you show?

options.text: Each class and offer has its own link that goes straight to payment
The embedded schedule, since it works the same way as his widget
The free app, since clients can’t book without downloading it
The community page, since posts there link to the full schedule

questions.reveal: Every class and offer has its own link, so a post, email or flyer can go straight to the purchase.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a real difference you can show against the Arketa checkout?

options.text: Booking with no account or password for a first-time client
Passing the card processing fee on to the client at checkout
Reserving a spot for a guest as part of the same booking flow
Showing packs and memberships to the client before checkout

questions.reveal: Arketa’s checkout made the client create an account with a password. It can pass fees on and book for a guest too.

questions.prompt: A spa owner who tried Arketa says booking red light plus sauna took two separate checkouts. What do you show?

options.text: The class schedule widget and how it matches her site’s brand
The Spot Filler sequence for filling her quieter time slots
Multi-service appointment checkout that books both together
The ads manager and how it tracks the leads from her Meta ads

questions.reveal: Book both services in one checkout. That was the reason one prospect left Arketa.

questions.prompt: A prospect says, “Arketa is the cheaper middle option, and it does sequences too.” What do you do?

options.text: Say Arketa is cheaper because it does about half of what we do
Grant what Arketa does well, then ask what it showed you haven’t
Match on price right away so the gap stops being an issue
List the bugs that other Arketa customers have told you about

questions.reveal: Conceding the basics and asking this surfaced the real deciding need in one cycle.

questions.prompt: A current Arketa customer says what keeps her there is asking her reports questions in plain language. What’s the right move?

options.text: Tell her it’s on the roadmap and should be live early next year
Show the reports library and say it does the same thing today
Say Arketa’s reporting is known to be off, so it won’t help her
Say honestly Momence has nothing equal to show; don’t promise a date

questions.reveal: Momence had no equivalent to show. Roadmap dates aren’t confirmed, so don’t name one.

questions.prompt: A Walla prospect asks why she’d use Momence’s pop-up instead of keeping booking on her site. What’s the strongest answer?

options.text: Nearly all clients prefer the pop-up, going by our own numbers
On-site booking is outdated, and Walla will move off it soon
Closing it returns them to the schedule, and each class has a link
There’s no real difference, so pick whichever one looks better

questions.reveal: Real reasons beat a made-up stat. And she can still embed the schedule if she prefers.

questions.prompt: Per the CC5 battle card, what’s the main angle against Walla?

options.text: Fees: Walla’s per-transaction charges on top of the subscription
Contracts: long Walla terms that are hard for studios to exit
Support: slow Walla replies when a studio needs help quickly
Consolidation: the other tools studios pay for alongside Walla

questions.reveal: There’s no fee angle on Walla. Ask what else they pay for to run email, texts and reviews.

questions.prompt: A prospect has demoed MindBody, Arketa, WellnessLiving and Mariana Tek, and has used Walla. What’s the best use of that?

options.text: Ask what each did well and what ruled it out, then demo to that
Walk through each one’s weak spots so she can rule them out
Skip it, since comparing platforms always looks defensive
Ask which was cheapest so you know the price you need to beat

questions.reveal: Her own reasons tell you which strengths to acknowledge and what to show first.

questions.prompt: Which landmine question matches a Walla prospect?

options.text: “Does your revenue report reconcile against Stripe?”
“What else do you pay for: email, SMS, reviews, forms?”
“If you cancelled tomorrow, would the charges stop?”
“What did your price move to at your last renewal?”

questions.reveal: Consolidation is the Walla angle. The others fit Arketa, WellnessLiving and Glofox.
